subject: Anchoring commitments and temporary cross-region hops — clarifications and evidence request
content:
From: Priya Das <legal@helixsys.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: cloud-compliance@helixsys.com
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Residency anchoring + temporary cross-region hops (initial questions)

Hi Sofia,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Helix is close on the legal review but we have two outstanding items before we can sign the DPA addendum:

1) Confirm the list of sub-processors that could touch Helix production data when region-anchoring is enabled (both primary and failover).
2) We need a clear definition of "temporary cross-region hop" (max duration, triggers, and audit evidence you provide).

Can you provide an evidence packet we can share with our internal Infosec and also confirm whether Redwood will accept a Helix requirement for KMS policy binding to the region (i.e., customer-managed keys that cannot be exported outside the pinned geography)?

Appreciate a response by EOD Friday — helps our board signoff timeline.

Best,
Priya
Legal — Helix Systems

---
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Das <legal@helixsys.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, cloud-compliance@helixsys.com
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Residency anchoring + temporary cross-region hops (initial questions)

Hi Priya — thanks for the clear ask. Short answers up front, full packet attached below.

- Sub-processors: primary serving and storage are Redwood-managed (our roster attached). In a pinned region configuration the only sub-processors that will ever hold plaintext customer content outside the pinned geography are the transient analytics pipeline and optional third-party telemetry partners — both of which we can opt out of in Dedicated/Private deployments. See the attached region_anchor_matrix.xlsx for full mapping.
- Temporary cross-region hops: defined as automated transient replication to a non-pinned region for < 30 minutes to support failover validation or cache population. Hops are only allowed when both (a) the customer has an active failover policy and (b) real-time capacity in the primary region is degraded. All hops are logged and we provide SHA-256 keyed evidence of the transfer.
- KMS: For Hosted customers we support a KMS integration that uses envelope encryption; keys remain in the customer-chosen cloud region. For Private deployments we support customer-managed HSM and strict geo-locked key policies. We cannot currently support a universal enforcement that prevents metadata/headers from being routed for control-plane purposes, but we do provide an evidentiary export and an optional escrow arrangement per contract.

I'm attaching: region_anchor_matrix.xlsx (roster + control-plane flows), kms_flowchart.png (how keys are applied), and a draft DPA addendum (DPA_addendum_draft_v3.pdf) with proposed language for transient hops and escrow.

Quick ask: Markus, Marissa — can you review the DPA wording in section 4.2 (transient replication) and confirm the audit evidence we can provide (signed hashes + transfer logs + time-limited access windows)? I want to be able to give Helix a concrete list of artifacts by EOD Friday.

Thanks,
Sofia
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

---
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 12:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Residency anchoring + temporary cross-region hops (initial questions)

Sofia — reviewed the addendum draft quickly. High-level: wording is fine but need to be explicit about SLA triggers for hop initiation. I propose:

- Trigger threshold: primary region CPU or network 85% sustained for 90s OR error-rate spike exceeding 5% across 5 mins.
- Max hop window: 30 minutes unless customer expressly approves extension via console (opt-in).
- Evidence package: (a) signed transfer manifest (hashed), (b) packet-level transfer log with timestamps, (c) snapshot of routing decision and autoscaler metric at the time.

I'll prepare a sample manifest and script to generate the signed hash; Marissa will attach the export sample.

—Markus
Director, Platform Reliability

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Das <legal@helixsys.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 3 Dec 2026 09:48:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Residency anchoring + temporary cross-region hops (initial questions)

Hi Priya — adding the sample evidence set and a short runbook for your SecOps team. Attached: region_anchor_matrix.xlsx (tab 3 has the subprocessor roster), kms_flowchart.png, and a one-page runbook PDF (link in Drive).

Short summary for SecOps:
- All transfers generate an immutable transfer manifest (sequence id, from_region, to_region, start_ts, end_ts, byte_count).
- We sign the manifest server-side with a per-tenant signing key and deliver the manifest and signed hash as part of the evidence packet.
- For Hosted customers who use Redwood KMS with regional key binding, keys are restricted to region by cloud IAM policy; Helix can optionally require yearly escrow rotation.

Priya — do you/your SecOps need us to ship a small script that validates the manifests against the signed hash? We can include it as an executable snippet in the Drive folder.

Cheers,
Marissa
Product — Security Integrations

From: Priya Das <legal@helixsys.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 3 Dec 2026 16:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Residency anchoring + temporary cross-region hops (initial questions)

Thanks — this is very helpful. A few follow-ups:

1) Can you confirm whether the signed manifest includes a non-repudiation timestamp tied to an internal HSM? Helix's SecOps requires our audit trail to be anchorable to an HSM-backed timestamp authority.
2) For the KMS escrow option: what format would the escrow keys be held in, and do you have an existing third-party escrow vendor you work with?
3) If a hop occurs during a customer-initiated legal hold, what protections prevent the transient copy from being accessible to third-party subprocessors?

If you can provide short answers + the sample validation script by EOD Friday we'll be able to push the addendum to signature next week.

Best,
Priya

---
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Das <legal@helixsys.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 4 Dec 2026 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Residency anchoring + temporary cross-region hops (initial questions)

Priya — quick answers and links to artifacts we dropped in the Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-helix-evidence

1) Timestamping / non-repudiation: our signing service is backed by an HSM (FIPS 140-2 Level 3) that emits a signed timestamp token (we include the token in the manifest). The token ties the manifest hash to an HSM-provisioned signing certificate; we can provide the cert chain and a sample verification script.

2) KMS escrow: escrowed key material is stored in a vendor-neutral PKCS#12 container and held with our compliance partner (we currently work with a named escrow provider; we'll include the redacted contract in the Drive packet). For Private deployments customers can opt for customer-run HSM + no-escrow.

3) Legal holds: temporary cross-region copies are subject to the same access controls as the primary copy; they are encrypted with the same per-tenant envelope key and access is restricted to a small, auditable set of process principals. We log all access and can produce access logs filtered by legal-hold tags. In the rare event a subprocess does need to run in the target region (e.g., node-level replication agent), we ensure it runs in an ephemeral sandbox with no persistent storage, and we can provide process-level attestation records.

Attached: sample_signed_manifest.json (manifest + signed token, redacted), validation_script.sh (small script; run locally), and DPA_addendum_v3_final.pdf (minor edits per Markus).

Let me know if Helix wants a short call to demo the verification flow; we can loop in engineering.

Thanks everyone —
Sofia
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
